summary:
B.R.A.S.A. (Regional Harmonized Satellite Fire Activity Log) is an interactive web application developed by CODE RED to transform fragmented satellite fire detection records into accessible and meaningful historical insights.
Using NASA FIRMS data from MODIS and VIIRS sensors, BRASA integrates satellite observations into a unified platform for exploring fire activity from 2001 to 2025. Through interactive maps, temporal visualizations, and geographical filters, users can analyze historical patterns, identify seasonal trends, and explore periods of unusual fire activity.
The project addresses the challenge of interpreting satellite records collected by different sensors, making historical fire information easier to understand and compare. Designed for emergency responders, researchers, and land managers, BRASA supports evidence-based decision-making, strengthens environmental monitoring, and contributes to a better understanding of fire activity across different regions.
details:
B.R.A.S.A. — Regional Harmonized Satellite Fire Activity Log

1. Project Overview

BRASA is an interactive web application developed by CODE RED to facilitate the exploration and interpretation of historical satellite-detected fire activity. The project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by bringing together observations from MODIS and VIIRS, accessible through NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS).

Satellite sensors have monitored active fire hotspots for more than two decades. However, differences in sensor characteristics, spatial resolution, and observation periods complicate historical comparisons. BRASA aims to make these records more accessible and understandable through an integrated geospatial and temporal exploration platform.

2. How Does BRASA Work?

BRASA provides an interactive interface where users can explore historical fire activity from 2001 to 2025.

Its main functionalities include:

  • Interactive geospatial maps: Visualize satellite-detected fire hotspots across selected geographical areas.
  • Geographical filters: Explore information by country, province, or canton.
  • Temporal exploration: Examine historical observations across different years and periods.
  • Sensor selection: Explore records associated with MODIS and VIIRS.
  • Historical analysis: Identify seasonal patterns, variations in detected fire activity, and periods that may require additional attention.

These features help transform complex satellite observations into information that users can explore without specialized geospatial programming knowledge.

3. NASA Data and Scientific Relevance

BRASA uses active fire detection records provided through NASA FIRMS, including observations from MODIS and VIIRS.

MODIS provides an extensive historical record, while VIIRS contributes observations with different spatial detection characteristics. Combining access to these datasets offers opportunities to examine fire activity across longer periods.

An important scientific consideration is that observations from different sensors are not automatically equivalent. Sensor sensitivity, spatial resolution, satellite coverage, and detection conditions may affect the results.

Furthermore, satellite-detected hotspots do not necessarily represent individual wildfire events. They may include agricultural burning and other thermal anomalies.

BRASA therefore emphasizes historical exploration and interpretation rather than treating hotspot counts as exact numbers of individual fires.

4. Benefits and Intended Impact

BRASA is designed to support three main groups:

Emergency responders: By examining historical patterns and identifying periods of increased detected fire activity, emergency teams can gain additional context for preparedness and monitoring.

Researchers: The platform facilitates the exploration of temporal trends, geographical distributions, and historical variability in satellite fire observations.

Land managers: Regional historical information can contribute to environmental monitoring, land management discussions, and informed planning.

The intended impact is to improve access to NASA's open satellite observations and support evidence-based understanding of fire activity.

5. Innovation and Creativity

BRASA's creative contribution lies in presenting historical satellite fire information through a unified, interactive experience.

Rather than requiring users to manually explore multiple datasets and interpret raw satellite records, the platform brings together maps, filters, and temporal visualizations in one accessible interface.

Its design emphasizes geographical exploration, historical context, and practical usability.

The project also connects scientific Earth observation resources with the needs of emergency responders, environmental researchers, and territorial decision-makers.

6. Development Approach and Technical Considerations

The project was developed as a web-based prototype integrating satellite fire observation datasets, geospatial visualization, and interactive data exploration.

The development process considered several important factors:

  • Differences between MODIS and VIIRS observations.
  • Availability and historical coverage of satellite data.
  • Geographical and temporal filtering.
  • Accessibility and clarity of information.
  • Usability for audiences with different technical backgrounds.
  • Responsible interpretation of satellite-detected hotspots.

The platform is intended to make complex Earth observation information easier to explore while maintaining awareness of the limitations of satellite fire detection.

7. Future Development

Future improvements could include more advanced sensor harmonization procedures, quantitative validation of historical comparisons, expanded geographical coverage, and analytical methods for identifying unusual fire activity.

These developments could strengthen BRASA's usefulness for environmental research and risk-informed monitoring.

8. Project Access and Source Code

Live Web Application:
https://brasa-web-code-red.onrender.com

Main GitHub Repository:
https://github.com/Susan9620/BRASA

Integration Repository:
https://github.com/leomezy21-coder/BRASA

Backend API:
https://brasa-api-mundial.onrender.com

BRASA provides a web-accessible interface supported by backend API services. Its source code is available through public GitHub repositories, enabling reviewers to examine the project's implementation and technical structure.

Conclusion

BRASA demonstrates how NASA's open satellite data can be transformed into an accessible digital tool for exploring historical fire activity.

By connecting MODIS and VIIRS observations with interactive maps and temporal analysis, CODE RED seeks to support a clearer understanding of fire patterns and contribute to more informed environmental decision-making.
